rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 The Deck 2.1 Number Cards 2.2 Action Cards 2.3 Modifier Cards 3 Gameplay 4 Game End Overview Flip 7 is a "push your luck" game a little like blackjack, but with exciting modifiers and actions to take against other players. The goal is to reach 200 points by taking cards (each card is worth its value), but if you get any duplicates, you bust and are out of the round. If you can successfully flip 7 (gain seven different number cards), you score 15 bonus points and end the round. The Deck The deck consists of 94 cards. Number Cards Most cards are number cards with values of 0 - 12. Twelve are 12 cards, eleven are 11 cards, ten are 10 cards, and so on down to one 1 card. There is also one 0 card. Note that the more valuable a card is, the more copies of it there are in the deck. Action Cards The deck contains three types of action cards. The player who draws an action card must choose a player (including themselves) to give it to. Freeze : Force a player to stay. They still score with their current cards. Flip Three : Force a player to draw three cards. If the chosen player draws a duplicate, they bust and don't draw any more. If the chosen player draws an action card, it is resolved after all three have been drawn. Second chance : A player who receives this gets to avoid busting once. The duplicate card and the Second Chance card are both discarded, and the player's turn continues. A player may hold only one Second Chance card. If another is drawn, it must be given to another player. Modifier Cards These cards add to your total score, but do not count towards a Flip 7 or a bust. The deck contains one each of +2 , +4 , +6 , +8 , +10 , and a multiplier card x2 Gameplay At the start of a round, each player is dealt one card. Then, in turn order, each player decides whether to hit (take a card) or stay (take no more cards and bank your points, which is the total of the value of the cards in front of you). If you hit, and that new card is a duplicate of one of your other number cards (not modifier cards), you have busted . This means you are out of the round and score zero points. The round ends when everyone has chosen to stay or has busted. If you manage to flip 7 unique number cards in a round, the round automatically ends. Each player who has not busted gains the points in front of them, and you gain 15 bonus points. Game End When at least one player reaches 200 points, the game ends and the player with the most points wins.

[Rating: 1/10] It's mildly amusing, but Knizia did this better and with more interaction in No Mercy. Or Circus Flohcati for a similar idea of avoiding doubles. Or Garfield's Grand Dalmuti for an inverted deck. And all of those create more silly player interaction than Flip 7, where everyone's playing solitaire.... until they get one of those attack cards and feel mildly uncomfortable that they have to hurt someone. Which is bizarre in a party game, 95% of this is training them to pretend the party doesn't exist (and these are random casual gamers who are otherwise huge fans of hurting each other!)  Also it'

[Rating: 1/10] It’s like they decided to plagerize the game Pairs but wanted to make it slower and less fun. Mission accomplished.

[Rating: 1/10] Can’t think why I would ever pick this over Pairs or Knizia’s Hit! Feels like an dishonest production.

[Rating: 1/10] Just roll a D6 each and move on. A really disappointing SdJ nominee which is fun in the same way as drawing & playing a +4 in Uno is fun.    The unique game design elements added to the base 'blackjack' mechanics (ie Freeze / Second chance cards) make it even more random.    There are plenty of push your luck games, social games, card games, pub games & filler games that are more worthy of recognition...

[Rating: 1/10] inconsequential game. I dont know why you would want to play it instead of doing anything else

[Rating: 1/10] Awful. I know it's supposed to be a simple push your luck game but this game offers ZERO choices except for should you stay or should you hit. That's really it. This is the push your luck equivalent of War. Just card flipping and randomness piled on top of randomness. And the box arrogantly claims itself as the best card game of all time. As if. I recommend Spots or Mystic Vale for a good push your luck game, as they feature both pushing your luck, as well as actual skill.

[Rating: 1/10] Enjoyable to play a few times, but far to luck based even for a push your luck game.  Downgraded my rating, the game does not reward pushing your luck. It rewards luck of getting the special cards. Such a shame as the concept is nice.

[Rating: 1/10] The positive thing I can say about this game is if it brings more people into the hobby I'm happy.  However, they could have sprung for  decent art, maybe a theme, this just lazy design. There are so many better games out there to play. I hope this game is soon forgotten.

[Rating: 1/10] Just reveal a card or pass and score. You can be left without playing by busting or someone else freezing you/making you bust.  Can't believe this was nominated for Spiel des Jahres. Besides, I read this was a copy of a variant of an old game.  Anyways, I just didn't find it fun due to its extreme simplicity along with the potential of not playing at all =S.

[Rating: 1/10] Ridiculous game, flip a card and hope you get something good. Pure luck.  Not only that, Soo many better versions of this style of game already exist.

[Rating: 1/10] Blackjack. But more boring and random.   My three friends played one hand and all agreed we never wanted to play this again. Fortunately it was at a game pub so no one had wasted money buying it
